de9_formation.topic: Peter Thiel: birth, childhood, schooling, Stanford, early career

claims.text: Born 11 October 1967 in Frankfurt am Main, West Germany, to Klaus Friedrich Thiel, a chemical engineer who worked for mining companies, and Susanne Thiel; family moved to Cleveland when he was one; to South West Africa (Namibia) in 1971, also lived in South Africa; settled in Foster City, California, 1977; changed elementary schools seven times; two years at a German-language school in Swakopmund, which he later linked to his dislike of regimentation; valedictorian San Mateo High School 1985

Stanford BA philosophy 1989; co-founded The Stanford Review 1987, first editor-in-chief until graduation; JD Stanford Law 1992; clerked for Judge James Larry Edmondson, 11th Circuit, 1992-93; securities lawyer at Sullivan & Cromwell, left in under a year; currency options derivatives trader at Credit Suisse from 1993; speechwriter for William Bennett; Thiel Capital Management founded with $1 million from friends and family (1996 per one passage)

Daily Maverick (citing Chafkin, The Contrarian, 2021): father Klaus, a mining project manager, worked on a uranium mine near Swakopmund; Thiel attended the whites-only Pridwin school in Johannesburg, then two years at the German School in Swakopmund; Chafkin: Thiel 'often spoke fondly of his childhood in South Africa'; two former peers recalled him saying 'It works' of apartheid and that denial of civil rights 'was economically sound'; his spokesperson denied these encounters

Lythcott-Haims (Stanford dorm mate 1985-86): Thiel told her 'moral issues were irrelevant' to the apartheid government's economy; Megan Maxwell: he said 'you shouldn't judge a government based on whether it fits your view of morality'; spokesperson: 'Peter has never supported apartheid, but he can easily see how a conversation might be misremembered 30 years later'

The Diversity Myth: Multiculturalism and Political Intolerance on Campus, by David O. Sacks and Peter A. Thiel, Independent Institute; argues Stanford's multiculturalism produced less learning, politicized curriculum, speech codes; book passage: a woman might 'realize' she had been 'raped' the next day; Thiel to CNNMoney (25 Oct 2016): 'More than two decades ago, I co-wrote a book with several insensitive, crudely argued statements'; 'I regret writing passages that have been taken to suggest otherwise'

de9_gawker.topic: Valleywag outing, Bollea v. Gawker funding, verdict, bankruptcy, op-ed

claims.text: Gawker published a 2007 post headlined 'Peter Thiel is totally gay, people'; Thiel confirmed to NYT (Sorkin) in May 2016 he paid about $10 million toward Terry Bollea's suit and others

Thiel to Sorkin: 'It's less about revenge and more about specific deterrence'; Gawker pioneered 'a unique and incredibly damaging way of getting attention by bullying people even when there was no connection with the public interest'; decided 'several years ago'; first step was hiring lawyers to find cases; 'It's safe to say this is not the only one'; Valleywag wrote antagonistic stories 'nearly a decade ago'
Thiel called the funding one of the 'greater philanthropic things that I've done' (26 May 2016)

Florida jury: Gawker liable $130 million, Nick Denton $10 million (March 2016, $140 million); settlement 'at least $31 million' per bankruptcy filings, 2 November 2016; Denton: 'The saga is over'; lawyer behind two other suits backed by Thiel

Gawker Media filed Chapter 11 in June 2016; Univision bid $135 million for six other sites; Gawker.com shutdown announced 18 August 2016, to stop within a week; Forbes: 'could serve as a blueprint for any billionaire who wants to lay siege against a media outlet'

Thiel NYT op-ed 15 August 2016: 'Protecting individual dignity online is a long-term project'; 'It is ridiculous to claim that journalism requires indiscriminate access to private people's sex lives'; would back Hogan until he wins and others in similar positions
Thiel (May 2009, to peHUB): 'Valleywag is the Silicon Valley equivalent of Al Qaeda'; 'I think they should be described as terrorists, not as writers or reporters'

de9_citizenship_tax.topic: New Zealand, German and Maltese citizenship; Roth IRA

claims.text: NZ citizenship granted 2011 at a private ceremony at the NZ consulate in Santa Monica; revealed by NZ Herald January 2017; application said he found 'no other country that aligns more with my view of the future than New Zealand' and it would give him 'great pride to let it be known that I am a New Zealand citizen'; said he would need to keep living in the US; minister Nathan Guy granted special approval citing his NZ venture fund (Xero) and 'million-dollar donation' to Christchurch earthquake relief; Lees-Galloway: 'entirely about money'; the 2011 documents show Thiel remained a German citizen

DIA: Thiel spent 'a total of 12 days' in NZ across four trips before citizenship (nine in the qualifying window), against a general requirement of 1,350 days over five years; approved under the 'exceptional circumstances' exemption; Guy: 'Exceptional circumstances are there for a reason'; Thiel declined to comment
NYT (Oct 2022): Thiel 'in the process of acquiring at least his third passport', Maltese, via the golden passport scheme; listed residence a 185-euro-a-night Airbnb; he declined to comment

ProPublica: January 1999 Thiel bought 1.7 million PayPal founders' shares at $0.001 each (~$1,700) in a Roth IRA; $1,664 at end-1999; about $5 billion at end-2019 across 96 subaccounts; 1999 income $73,263 under the $110,000 limit; Fleischer: 'That's a huge scandal'; Baker: can't support the valuation; Pensco founder: 'very legitimate'; IRS audit opened 2011, closed with no additional tax, records don't show if Roth involved; moved to Rivendell trust 2018; 2005 NZ residency application letter: 'Mr. Thiel purchased his founders' shares in PayPal through his Roth IRA'; spokesman accepted questions but never responded; ProPublica says the purchase 'risked running afoul' of rules, reaches no legal conclusion

de9_companies.topic: PayPal, Clarium, Palantir, Facebook, Founders Fund, Mithril, Valar

claims.text: Thiel provided the initial $100,000 for Fieldlink in 1998; Confinity launched PayPal in 1999; IPO 15 February 2002; eBay bought PayPal for $1.5 billion in October 2002; Thiel's 3.7% stake worth about $55 million; CEO until the sale

X.com and Confinity merged March 2000 under the X.com name; September 2000 executives delivered no-confidence letters as Musk left on a fundraising trip and honeymoon; board replaced Musk with Thiel as CEO (Vance 2015; Inc. 2007)

Clarium Capital founded with $10 million of PayPal proceeds as a global macro fund; +57.1% 2005, -7.8% 2006, +40.3% 2007; assets over $7 billion by Q1 2008; $350 million by 2011, about two-thirds Thiel's own money
Palantir incorporated May 2003; Thiel and his fund largely funded the initial $30 million; In-Q-Tel invested about $2 million; Thiel chairman

Facebook: August 2004 $500,000 for 10.2% (first outside investment, company valued $4.9 million); sold 16.8 million shares for $638 million at the May 2012 IPO and most of the rest in August 2012 for about $395.8 million, total above $1 billion; left Meta board after 17 years (announced 7 February 2022) to support 2022 candidates

Founders Fund founded 2005 by Thiel, Ken Howery and Luke Nosek with a $50 million first fund; first institutional investor in SpaceX (from 2008, Nosek led) and Palantir; about $17 billion under management by 2025; $1 billion into Anduril's 2025 Series G, its largest ever (source does not say who led); Valar Ventures co-founded 2010; Mithril Capital launched June 2012 with a $402 million fund

de9_politics.topic: Thiel political money and positions 2012-2026; Argentina; Antichrist lectures

claims.text: RNC 21 July 2016: 'I am proud to be gay. I am proud to be a Republican. But most of all I am proud to be an American'; 'fake culture wars' 'distract us from our economic decline'; 'Our nuclear bases still use floppy disks'; Trump 'is a builder'

Thiel pledged $1.25 million to help elect Trump in the campaign's final weeks (Oct 2016); named to the Presidential Transition Team Executive Committee (announced 11 November 2016); Thiel: 'Most Americans don't live by the [Washington] Beltway or San Francisco Bay'

2022: Thiel gave $15 million to the pro-Vance super PAC in the Ohio primary; $15 million to the pro-Masters super PAC in the Arizona primary and $2.5 million in October (FEC); total about $32 million in the midterms; Vance won, Masters lost

Ballotpedia: 2015 $2 million to a pro-Fiorina super PAC; 2018 $1 million Club for Growth Action, $100,000 CLF; 2020 more than $2 million to Free Forever PAC (Kobach) and $100,000 SLF; Forbes: $35 million across 16 federal races in 2022; 2024 cycle: 'over $1.7 million to candidates for federal office and political parties' per FEC records (not itemized)

Reuters 26 April 2023 (two people close to him): Thiel did not plan to donate to candidates in 2024; unhappy with GOP focus on cultural issues; might still support former employees; declined interview
Gellman (Atlantic, Nov 2023) paraphrase: Thiel wanted published that he 'wouldn't be giving money to any politician, including Donald Trump, in the next presidential campaign'
Aspen Ideas, June 2024: 'If you hold a gun to my head, I'll vote for Trump'; 'I'm not going to give any money to his super PAC'
Thiel told the Atlantic voting for Trump 'was like a not very articulate scream for help'; turned down a $10 million request from the Trump campaign; Vance (FT) urged him to 'get off the sidelines'
February 2025: $852,200 to Grow the Majority, Speaker Mike Johnson's committee; Mother Jones says he 'sat out' 2024
February 2026: $1.5 million to Club for Growth Action per FEC filing; Bloomberg: 'ramping up his engagement with federal politics again after sitting out the 2024 election cycle'
29 December 2025: $3 million to the California Business Roundtable to fight the proposed 5% one-time billionaire tax (2026 Billionaire Tax Act)

Thiel Capital opened a Miami office (Dec 2025); Miami Beach mansion since 2020; moved voter registration to Florida March 2024 per state records; NYT: Thiel among those looking to cut California ties by year end

Milei met Thiel at the Casa Rosada 23 April 2026 with Foreign Minister Quirno; Milei: 'wonderful meeting', both view 'taxes as theft', Thiel 'an anarcho-capitalist, just as I am'; no specific investments discussed; first visit May 2024 with Alec Oxenford; reported US$12 million mansion in Palermo Chico

NYT 28 May 2026: Thiel bought a Buenos Aires mansion; government reportedly considering residence or citizenship; Milei spokesperson denied; reasons reported include concern over US direction, the California tax, backup countries
Fortune 16 July 2026: Thiel relocated with his family to Buenos Aires earlier that summer; Argentina's citizenship-by-investment programme not yet live

Argentine Chamber of Deputies held a hearing (about 28 August 2026) on Thiel's presence and ties to Milei's government; Thiel invited but did not appear; Palantir registered with INPI in 2022 and showed interest in digitising AMIA archives; no Palantir contracts with Argentina reported
Antichrist lectures: four private, off-record sessions at the Commonwealth Club, San Francisco, September-October 2025, organised by Acts 17 Collective, drawing on Girard

Fortune Dec 2024: Jim O'Neill, former CEO of Thiel's foundation, picked for deputy HHS secretary; Michael Kratsios, Thiel Capital's former chief of staff, handling tech policy; Sacks AI and crypto czar; Thiel introduced Vance to Trump in 2021; Vance worked at Mithril
Fortune May 2025: Ken Howery, Founders Fund co-founder, nominated ambassador to Denmark; a Thiel protégé directs OSTP

Masters was president of the Thiel Foundation from 2015 and chief operating officer and special counsel at Thiel Capital from 2018; co-wrote Zero to One (2014) with Thiel; campaign said he would resign from Thiel Capital before the primary
Thiel spent $15 million to support Masters in the GOP primary; offered SLF a matched deal of at least $10 million combined, Thiel paying half

Mother Jones: Palantir had more than $113 million in new and previous federal contracts under the second Trump administration as of early May 2025 (per NYT) and a $795 million Defense Department AI software deal that could rise to $1.3 billion; Grow the Majority passed funds to the NRCC and to Republicans in competitive districts
